questions.question: For the ten scores with sum 570, the mean is:
With Q1 = 47 and Q3 = 69, the lower fence Q1 − 1,5 × IQR equals:
The minimum 15 lies above the fence of 14, so the correct conclusion is:
options: 15 is an outlier — it looks far from the data
No outlier — the calculation, not the eye, decides
15 must be removed from the data

questions.question: Predicting umbrella sales at 60 mm from data observed between 5 and 30 mm is:
options: Extrapolation — calculate if asked, then decline to trust it

subtopics.title: Analytical Geometry — the Grid and Its Four Formulas

questions.question: With A(−2; 7) and B(4; −1), the gradient, midpoint and length of AB are:
With gradient −4/3, the angle of inclination is:
options: 126,87° — add 180° to the calculator's negative angle

questions.question: Completing the square on x² + y² − 4x + 10y + 4 = 0 gives:
At (5; −1) on that circle, the tangent's gradient is −3/4 because:
options: The point is below the x-axis
The radius gradient is 4/3 and tangent ⊥ radius

questions.question: cos 105° = cos(60° + 45°) evaluates exactly to:
options: (√2 − √6)/4 — negative, as the second quadrant demands

questions.question: With cos x = 3/5 and x acute, the pair (sin 2x; cos 2x) is:
In proving sin 2x/(1 + cos 2x) = tan x, the face of cos 2x that kills the one is:
Sides 6 and 10 enclosing 120° give a third side of:
A central angle of 140° forces an angle at the circumference on the same arc of:
options: 70° — angle at centre equals two times angle at circumference

questions.question: A diameter in a rider diagram 'whispers':
options: Ninety degrees — angle in a semicircle

questions.question: In a similarity ratio, the order of the letters naming the triangles matters because:
options: The order IS the mapping — scrambled order scrambles the ratio

questions.question: A correct geometry statement with a missing or invented reason:
options: Loses the reason's mark — statement and reason are paid as a pair

questions.question: Statistics should be banked early and cleanly because:
options: It is routine calculator work, and finishing it settles the pulse for the geometry
It cannot be returned to later
The calculator switches off after an hour

questions.question: Trigonometry revision 'compounds' because:
options: It has the most formulas to memorise
Identities, equations and triangle rules share one small toolkit
The calculator does most of it

questions.question: On this material, every question should begin with:
options: Drawing or completing the diagram and labelling everything given

subtopics.title: The Formula Toolkit — What Must Live in Your Head

questions.question: The judgement layer that no reference material can carry for you includes:
options: Quadrant signs, reduction rules, special angles, and theorem reason wordings

questions.question: Retrieval beats recognition because:
options: Producing a formula on a blank page survives the exam room; nodding at one does not

questions.question: The recommended toolkit drill is:
options: Copying formulas from notes into a new book
One page written from memory every second day, then tested against worked examples
Highlighting the formula list in colour

subtopics.title: Reasons, Rounding and the Paper Two Habits

questions.question: The two-second glance that protects a dozen trigonometry marks is:
options: Checking the calculator is in degree mode

questions.question: When a question asks for cos 105° in surd form, a calculator decimal:
options: Earns nothing — the exact value is the answer

questions.question: The 'diagram as ledger' habit means:
options: Keeping the diagram unlabelled for neatness
Writing every discovered fact onto the diagram immediately, for later parts to spend

questions.question: For trigonometric equations, the correct order is:
options: Interval first, then the general solution
Family first with its k, then harvest the members inside the interval
